title: Add unit tests for `FontVariation`
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

`FontVariation` is listed as lacking test coverage in #43440 and currently has none. This adds tests for its property accessors, its change-notification behaviour, and — using a variable font — the OpenType variation axes themselves.

## Additional information

### Test data

No font currently in the repository exposes variation axes, so this adds an ASCII subset of the variable Inter font (41 KB) as `tests/data/fonts/InterVariable-ASCII.woff2`, with a matching `COPYRIGHT.txt` entry. It deliberately lives in the test data rather than in `thirdparty/fonts`, which `editor/themes/SCsub` globs into the editor binary.

### Behaviour covered

- **OpenType variation axes change glyph metrics** — a `wght` of 900 measures wider than a `wght` of 100, and distinct coordinates resolve to distinct font RIDs.
- **Embolden changes glyph metrics** — at the strength the editor theme itself uses to synthesize its bold font.
- **Spacing changes measured size** — glyph spacing applies to the 8 glyphs of `"Test text"` but not to its space, space spacing only to the space, and top/bottom spacing to the line height rather than the width.
- **Without modifications it measures like its base font.**
- **Changed signal is only emitted when a value differs** — every `FontVariation` setter is guarded by an inequality check before `_invalidate_rids()`, so a redundant set must not invalidate the cached RIDs or emit `changed`.
- **Changes to the base font are propagated** — `set_base_font()` connects to the base font's `changed` signal and disconnects it on replacement.
- **Dictionaries are stored as copies** — `set_variation_opentype()` and `set_opentype_features()` call `duplicate()`, so mutating the caller's dictionary afterwards must not reach into the font.
- **Reset state** — `reset_state()` restores defaults and clears the base font, reached through a `Resource` handle the way resource reloading reaches it.
- **Default values** and property round-trips.

Metrics produced by Godot's own arithmetic are asserted exactly; metrics that depend on FreeType rasterisation are asserted relationally, so the tests do not become platform-sensitive.

### Verification

Built and run on Windows: 11 cases / 68 assertions for `FontVariation`, and the full suite at 1432 cases / 424299 assertions, both passing.

---

> [!NOTE]
> *AI disclosure*: I used Claude Code to help draft these tests. I reviewed every assertion against `scene/resources/font.h` and `scene/resources/font.cpp`, and verified all of them by building and running the test suite locally.
